reviewer: Amp local source review with focused Oracle consultation; not independent external review
review_scope: Clarify Order, Configuration and indexed State without changing their contracts; distinguish persistent Configuration comparisons from cross-State reidentification. Aesthetics results are separate evidence, not asserted green here.

findings.resolution: Order is explicitly the member-Set/extension pair, not the member Set. Direction's extension need not be the strict part of an Order; the contradictory phrase strict Order is removed. OC-D1 and OC-C1 retain the same partial-order laws, strict-part laws and asymmetric nontransitive counterexample.

State is a Configuration-position pair whose Identity compares both components. Configuration Identity still compares members and selected associations. One Configuration at two positions therefore gives different States, matching OC-D2 and OC-C2 rather than contradicting extensional Configuration Identity.

Persistence now assigns a Configuration to each State rather than indexing Configurations by States. Its pointwise member/structure/Identity statements do not determine cross-State reidentification. Entity carries State Configurations without becoming any one of them. All Lean sources and nine OC contracts are unchanged; the 58-job build and finite executable pass.

Interpretation predicates, empirical identity criteria, actual ordered-pair applications, finite-arity coverage and full Perception/Memory parity remain the existing OC-G1 application gates. Neither these prose clarifications nor Aesthetics judgments discharge them.
